steps: Here we have your code, an agent, a folder of invoices and a database. Without a schema, the agent answers in prose, and your code is left trying to regex the amount out of free text. That is fragile text parsing.
So instead, your code calls query with an output format: a J S O N schema of exactly three fields, vendor, amount and due date. The agent now knows the shape its answer must take.
Next, the prompt says extract the fields from the invoice text file, so the agent uses the Read tool, the only tool it is allowed, and the invoice text comes back.

Now the agent produces its J S O N object, with vendor Acme and amount twelve hundred and fifty, and it validates against the schema. If it kept failing, you would get a max structured output retries error instead.
The validated object arrives in the result message as structured output. Notice it is already a dictionary, not a string, and the run finishes with a success subtype.
Finally, typed data just works. Your code adds ten percent tax, giving thirteen hundred and seventy-five, and writes one clean row to the database. Schemas replace scraping.
